Connect the speaker you want to calibrate via Bluetooth, AUX cable, USB or HDMI and play something briefly to check it works. Headphones are blocked on purpose – AutoVybz is made for loudspeakers.

• Put the phone where you usually listen (sofa, desk chair) at about ear height.
• The main microphone is usually at the bottom edge – point it towards the speaker.
• Distance: 1–2 m for room speakers, 50–80 cm for small desktop speakers.
• Lay the phone on something soft or a stack of books, not directly on a table (reflections).
• Don't hold it in your hand – your body changes the sound.
AutoVybz sets the phone\'s media volume to about 70 %. Set the speaker itself to a normal, comfortable listening level. If the result says “overloaded”, turn down; if it says “quiet”, turn up.
Close windows, switch off fans or the dishwasher and don\'t talk during the 10 seconds. AutoVybz measures the background noise first and warns you if it was too loud.

Dolby Atmos, “Adapt Sound”, bass boost or the EQ in your speaker\'s app change what AutoVybz measures. Turn them off before measuring – you can switch them on again later. The AutoVybz EQ pauses itself automatically.

Bluetooth adds 100–300 ms delay. AutoVybz finds the exact delay itself, so you don\'t need to do anything. Many party speakers have built-in bass boost that changes with volume – calibrate at the volume you usually use.

Every calibrated speaker gets its own profile – switch between them on the Sound screen (e.g. Bluetooth speaker at home and party speaker outdoors). On top you pick a style such as Hip-hop & R&B, Reggae & dancehall, Rock or Live & concert. Styles are gentle curves of at most ±6 dB that sit on top of the calibration; Strength sets how much. Bass and treble in the Studio add your personal touch. AutoVybz lowers the pre-gain automatically, so no combination can distort.

The speaker plays pink noise and a logarithmic sine sweep (20 Hz – 20 kHz) for exactly 10 seconds while the phone records. AutoVybz calculates the frequency response, compensates the typical behaviour of phone microphones, smooths it (stronger in the bass, ⅓ octave in mids and highs) and fits up to 10 parametric filters that bring your speaker towards the chosen target. A negative pre-gain and the limiter prevent clipping.

Phone microphones are not measurement microphones; the built-in profiles are estimates. Deep bass the speaker physically can\'t play is never boosted (protects the speaker). For lab-grade results use a USB measurement microphone with its calibration file (Studio).
AutoVybz is 100 % open source (GPL-3.0). Free is intentionally limited; AutoVybz Pro removes the limits. No tracking, no account.

Pre-gain %1$s dB: outdoors AutoVybz boosts by 3 dB at most and prefers cutting, and the loudness compensation keeps the level up for the party.
The limiter is switched on automatically when you activate this calibration and protects the speaker at party volume.
Party tip: extra bass comes free with placement – put the speaker on the ground (up to +6 dB) or close to a wall. Then measure again.
Outdoors a single position is unreliable (ground reflection). With 3 positions the result gets much more accurate.

Outdoors there are no walls – that changes the acoustics completely. Choose “Outdoors · Party” in the wizard:
• Less bass: indoors the walls lift the bass by about 4–8 dB; outdoors that is missing. Making up for it with EQ costs exactly as much loudness and strains the woofer. That is why outdoor mode boosts by 3 dB at most and prefers cutting. Extra bass comes free with placement: speaker on the ground (up to +6 dB), close to a wall or a house corner (even more).
• Ground reflection: sound bouncing off the ground cancels single frequencies, depending on where you stand. No EQ can fill these holes – AutoVybz ignores them and averages 3 positions. Spread them 1–2 m apart over the area where people will be.
• Wind & noise: wind on the microphone causes strong bass rumble. Turn the microphone opening away from the wind, put a thin cloth over it and wait for a calm moment. Frequencies where wind, traffic, birds or cicadas are louder than the speaker are automatically left uncorrected – the result shows which ones.
• Distance & level: measure 2–4 m in front of the speaker, turned up properly (party level, but not maximum – many party speakers turn their bass down there).
• Bluetooth range: outdoors no walls reflect the signal. Keep the phone near the speaker; dropouts are detected.
• Two speakers / party mode: measure each speaker on its own or put them close together – two speakers far apart cause strong interference outdoors.
• Sun: in outdoor mode AutoVybz turns the screen brightness up during the calibration. The limiter is always switched on when activating.

Choose the speaker type for weak or cheap speakers and measure as usual. AutoVybz then works more decisively: boomy bass and harsh mids are cut deeper, missing treble is lifted broadly, and a protective high-pass removes deep bass that the little driver cannot reproduce – on its own that takes away most rattling and distortion and leaves room for cleaner loudness. Physics stays physics: real deep bass will not appear, but balanced and clear is very much possible.

The speaker type for this device measures the built-in speakers with the built-in microphone: disconnect all external outputs and lay the device screen-up on a table. Because the microphone sits only a few centimetres from the speaker, AutoVybz corrects gently and only up to 12 kHz – but it removes the inaudible deep bass that only makes small speakers distort, tames the typical shouty mids and keeps the limiter armed. The result is a normal profile; switch profiles when you connect an external speaker again.
